title: Orthogonal estimation research basis

research_setting.statement_markdown: Develop an estimator of a parameter $\theta_0$ defined by $\mathbb E[\psi(W;\theta_0,\eta_0)]=0$ under stated nuisance-estimation and identification assumptions.

phase2_preparation.instructions_markdown: Propose and compare methods for the stated moment problem; distinguish mathematical definition from unestablished claims.

landscape.summary_markdown: The retained source supplies the orthogonal-score foundation.

topics.title: Orthogonal estimating equations
topics.description_markdown: Moment equations insensitive to first-order nuisance perturbations.

frameworks.title: Orthogonal population moments
frameworks.formulation_markdown: Let $\theta_0$ satisfy $\mathbb E[\psi(W;\theta_0,\eta_0)]=0$. Neyman orthogonality requires $\left.\partial_t\mathbb E[\psi(W;\theta_0,\eta_0+t h)]\right|_{t=0}=0$ for admissible nuisance directions $h$.
frameworks.assumptions_markdown: The target $\theta_0$ is identified by the population moment. The derivative exists for the declared admissible nuisance directions $h$; integrability and regularity must be stated for any inference claim.
frameworks.explanation_markdown: Nuisance perturbations have no first-order effect on the identifying population moment at the target.
frameworks.relevance_markdown: Separates the target-defining condition from the construction and estimation of nuisance functions.
limitations: Structural illustration using the existing source fixture, not a new scientific finding.

variants.title: Vector-valued orthogonal moments
variants.formulation_markdown: For $\psi=(\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_q)^\top$, require $$\mathbb E[\psi(W;\theta_0,\eta_0)]=0\in\mathbb R^q,\qquad \left.\frac{d}{dt}\mathbb E[\psi_j(W;\theta_0,\eta_0+t h)]\right|_{t=0}=0,\quad j=1,\ldots,q.$$
variants.assumptions_markdown: Each component moment and directional derivative exists. Identification must be established for the chosen parameter dimension and moment system.
variants.explanation_markdown: The same local sensitivity requirement is imposed component by component.
variants.changes_markdown: Replace a scalar score by a declared $q$-dimensional score, without dropping the local derivative condition.
variants.consequences_markdown: A vector equation needs an identified solution and, when overidentified, a specified estimation criterion; orthogonality alone does not choose that criterion.
limitations: Structural illustration using the existing source fixture, not a new scientific finding.

relationships.title: Scalar as a componentwise special case
relationships.formulation_markdown: Setting $q=1$ in $\mathbb E[\psi(W;\theta_0,\eta_0)]=0\in\mathbb R^q$ and its componentwise directional derivative condition yields the scalar moment and derivative equations.
relationships.assumptions_markdown: Use the same distribution, parameter, nuisance class, admissible directions and regularity assumptions on both sides; no estimator or rate equivalence is asserted.
relationships.explanation_markdown: This comparison concerns the dimension of the equations. It does not establish equality of statistical procedures or guarantees.
limitations: Structural illustration using the existing source fixture, not a new scientific finding.

algorithm_families.title: Cross-fitted estimating equations
algorithm_families.formulation_markdown: Let $I_1,\ldots,I_K$ partition $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and let $\widehat\eta_{-k}$ be fit without fold $I_k$. A pooled estimating equation is $$\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i\in I_k}\psi(W_i;\widehat\theta,\widehat\eta_{-k})=0.$$ The score and a rule for choosing a solution must be specified.
algorithm_families.assumptions_markdown: The sample structure must permit the declared split, the nuisance fits and moments must be well defined, and sufficient nuisance rates and identification are needed for any asymptotic claim.
algorithm_families.explanation_markdown: Nuisance fitting and moment evaluation use separate folds. This is an estimation construction associated with the moment setting, not a different target definition.
algorithm_families.computational_requirements_markdown: Fit nuisance functions on $K$ training complements and solve the pooled moment system. Cost depends on the nuisance learner, score evaluation and root solver.
limitations: Structural illustration using the existing source fixture, not a new scientific finding.

attention_items.question: Which admissible nuisance class is part of the requested setting?
attention_items.likely_consequence: The admissible nuisance class determines the shared assumptions and which published results apply.
attention_items.context_markdown: The requested setting defines $\theta_0$ by $\mathbb E[\psi(W;\theta_0,\eta_0)]=0$, where $W$ is the observed random vector, $\theta_0$ the target and $\eta_0$ a nuisance function. The source `citation.orthogonal_scores.2018` motivates sensitivity to admissible nuisance perturbations. Should the setting require a specified parametric class $\eta_0\in\{\eta_\beta:\beta\in\mathbb R^d\}$, or a declared nonparametric function class $\eta_0\in\mathcal H$? Please specify the intended class and associated regularity assumptions. This changes the common setting for every proposed method; it does not ask the researcher to derive an algorithm.

changes.limitations_markdown: Identification, moment regularity and appropriate nuisance convergence remain necessary; the equation alone is not a finite-sample guarantee. A local derivative condition is not a claim of global nuisance invariance.

entry_corrections.reason_markdown: Make the local scope explicit without changing the authored derivative condition. This fixture demonstrates revision provenance; it is not a newly performed source audit.
